paper_title: IPS Lower Bounds for Formulas and Sum of ROABPs
classifications: Theory of computation → Algebraic complexity theory
statement: Finally, we state a few open problems for further study. 1. Prove (nearly) quadratic-size IPSLin′ lower bounds for formulas for an axiom polynomial which is sparse. 2. Prove super-linear size mult-IPSLin′ and IPSLin′ lower bounds for ABPs and circuits. Again, the axiom polynomials should be sparse. 3. Can we (re)-prove Theorem A.5 for a sparse axiom polynomial?
context: However, if one does not care about constructing sparse axiom polynomials, then the problem of proving polynomial-size quality lower bounds for formulas, ABPs, and circuits can be solved easily. This is noted in Observation B.2. As already mentioned above, it is more desirable if IPS lower bound results are shown for sparse axioms. This is also reflected if one compares the work of [3] with [22]. Finally, we state a few open problems for further study. 1. Prove (nearly) quadratic-size IPSLin′ lower bounds for formulas for an axiom polynomial which is sparse. 2. Prove super-linear size mult-IPSLin′ and IPSLin′ lower bounds for ABPs and circuits. Again, the axiom polynomials should be sparse. 3. Can we (re)-prove Theorem A.5 for a sparse axiom polynomial?
